chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhary, from Abdul Samad ibn Basheer, from Suleyman ibn Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who does it with the man.

He said: If it was without penetration, then whipping; and if it was with penetration, stand him up straight, then strike with the sword with one strike. The sword takes from him what it takes. So I said to him, 'It is the killing.' He said, 'It is that.'

key_terms.الثَّقْب: Penetration (specifically in the context of sodomy)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in penalty for sodomy based on the degree of penetration in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the distinction in the hadd penalty for liwat based on the depth of penetration, prescribing flogging for partial entry and execution via a single sword strike for full penetration. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that this specific method of execution is legally considered 'qatl' (killing), distinguishing it from other forms of capital punishment. This ruling reflects the juristic consensus on the severity of the act, treating it with the gravity of a capital offense when consummated.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Abdul Samad Bin Basheer, from Suleyman Bin Hilal, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who did it with the man,

so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was without the penetration, so the whipping, and if it was with the penetration, stand him up straight, then strike with the sword with one strike. The sword takes from him what it takes’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘It is the killing’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is that’.
